source.title: A predictive coding account of bistable perception - a model-based fMRI study

confidence_rationale: A computational + model-based-fMRI account in which endogenous perceptual switches are DRIVEN by prediction errors accruing from residual evidence for the currently-suppressed interpretation, outperforming classic adaptation/noise models and localising the PE signal to frontal cortex. This is the closest mechanistic analogue of MECH-456's asserted trigger: the competitor overtakes when the current configuration accrues prediction error. The predictive-coding framing is also architecturally congenial to REE. Held below 0.8 because bistable perception switches between two fixed interpretations of a CONSTANT ambiguous stimulus with no ground-truth winner, whereas MECH-456 requires an exogenous ground-truth overtake -- the trigger transfers cleanly, the 'which is correct' semantics do not.
failure_signatures: Bistable perception has no ground-truth correct percept -- switching is endogenous and either interpretation is 'right'. MECH-456's rebinding must track a TRUE competitor that genuinely becomes better-supported by the environment; the paper's mechanism explains switching-on-PE but not tracking-the-true-winner (that is DV1 of the functional test, un-addressed here).
The PE signal was localised to inferior frontal gyri / anterior insula via model-based fMRI regressors -- correlational, and in a perceptual-report task, not a self<->world-config binding.
Model comparison favoured predictive coding over adaptation+noise, but bistable dynamics are notoriously fit by multiple models; the win is evidential, not decisive.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Endogenous perceptual transitions in bistable vision are caused by prediction errors that emerge from residual evidence for the currently-suppressed percept. A Bayesian predictive-coding model reproduces the temporal statistics of bistability, its stabilisation parameter predicts individuals' switch frequency, it outperforms adaptation/noise/adaptation+noise models in formal comparison, and its prediction-error time-course correlates with frontal (IFG/anterior insula) BOLD.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the mechanistic core of MECH-456's rebinding TRIGGER. The claim asserts the competitor world-configuration overtakes 'when the current config accrues prediction-error', and that the switch is prediction-error / competitor-overtake driven rather than a coherence-specific selection factor. Weilnhammer et al. supply exactly that mechanism in a biological + computational setting: accumulating prediction error for the suppressed alternative drives the switch, and a stabilisation parameter (the hysteresis MECH-456 also needs) governs how readily it fires. The predictive-coding / Bayesian framing maps naturally onto REE's E(tau) prediction-error machinery on which the claim's grounding rests.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Bistable perception switches between two FIXED interpretations of a constant ambiguous stimulus with NO ground-truth winner -- the PE trigger transfers, but the paper cannot speak to MECH-456's DV1 (rebinding tracks the TRUE competitor above a shuffle control), because in bistability there is no true competitor to track. The neural localisation is correlational fMRI in a perceptual-report task, not a latent binder.
mapping.source_context: Human model-based fMRI; binocular-rivalry / ambiguous-structure bistable perception with Bayesian predictive-coding model fitting and formal model comparison.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (PLoS Comput Biol, model comparison + fMRI validation). Mapping fidelity good (0.7): PE-accrual-drives-switch is very nearly MECH-456's stated trigger, and the stabilisation parameter mirrors the rebinding threshold. Transfer risk moderate (0.35): endogenous bistable switching with no ground-truth winner vs exogenous ground-truth overtake -- trigger transfers, correctness semantics do not.
